edits.before: Choose sunny, fertile, well-drained soil, pH 6–7. Chicory also tolerates modest fertility; heavy feeding is unnecessary.
edits.after: Choose sunny, fertile, well-drained soil; heavy feeding is unnecessary.

edits.before: Deep, loose soil gives straight forcing roots that lift undamaged in autumn.
edits.after: Loosen soil deeply so forcing roots grow straight and lift undamaged.

edits.before: Add mature compost where humus is low. Rake a fine seedbed just before sowing; use organic feed only on poor soil.
edits.after: Add mature compost where humus is low. Rake a fine seedbed; feed only poor soil.

edits.before: For baby leaves, thin to 2 in.. Give forcing roots and heads their wider spacings in Quick facts.
edits.after: Thin baby leaves to 2 in.; use Quick facts for roots and heads.

edits.before: For baby leaves, thin to 5 cm. Give forcing roots and heads their wider spacings in Quick facts.
edits.after: Thin baby leaves to 5 cm; use Quick facts for roots and heads.

edits.before: Hoe regularly and water new seedlings and established plants in dry spells. Eat useful thinnings.
edits.after: Hoe regularly and water in dry spells, especially young seedlings. Eat useful thinnings.

edits.before: Pick green leaves for summer salads as needed. Cut non-forcing heads in autumn; use promptly or keep cool, and protect crops left standing from frost.
edits.after: Pick green salad leaves as needed. Cut non-forcing heads in autumn; use promptly or keep cool. Protect standing crops from frost.

edits.before: Chicons are usually ready after three or four weeks of forcing. Cut or break them just above the crown without damaging the root.
edits.after: Chicons usually take three or four weeks of forcing. Cut or break just above the crown, leaving the root intact.

edits.before: For a smaller second crop, water compost and replace the dark cover. Keep harvested chicons dark: light makes them greener and more bitter.
edits.after: Water and cover again for a possible smaller second crop. Keep harvested chicons cool and dark to limit greening and bitterness.

sow: Space seeds thinly in drills about {½ in.~1 cm} deep and cover with fine soil. Use forcing varieties such as Witloof for winter chicons; other types form outdoor heads.
steps: Lift forcing roots in November. Keep sound roots at least {1 in.~2.5 cm} across the crown (the top of the root); discard weak, badly forked or rotten ones. Trim leaves to {1 in.~2.5 cm} above the crown, keeping the growing point.

Stand a few roots upright, close together, in a deep pot of moist compost, with crowns exposed. Shorten roots only if needed to fit. Store the rest horizontally in sand in a cool shed for later batches.
Cover with an upturned opaque bucket or large pot. Block holes in the cover and leave room for shoots. Keep in complete darkness at {50–59°F~10–15°C}.
